title: The Governed Agent Office
pitch: Combine OpenRig's persistent multi-agent 'teams' (coding owner, reviewer, and specialist seats that remember context across days) with OpenShell's policy-enforced sandboxing (every file, network call, and credential locked to an explicit allowlist) to build a product for companies whose security teams won't let them run autonomous AI agents at all. Each OpenRig seat runs inside its own OpenShell sandbox with a reviewed policy, so a finance-automation agent can touch the accounting API and nothing else, and a code-reviewer agent can read the repo but never push without human sign-off. Sell it to mid-size companies as 'the agent team your compliance department will actually approve' — a persistent, role-based AI workforce that's auditable file-by-file and call-by-call instead of one unrestricted terminal session.
why_now: Multi-agent setups like OpenRig are trending because one agent isn't enough for real work, but every enterprise rollout stalls on the same objection: how do we stop it from doing something we didn't approve? OpenShell answering that exact question on the same day means the missing piece for enterprise-grade autonomous agent teams just showed up.
